verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents its own secrets-management layer: SecretRefs so credentials need not sit as plaintext in config, plus a shared secret store, runtime snapshots and one-way scrubbing, which covers the store and redaction parts of the story. Isolated cells and agents also keep separate credentials and auth. Coverage is limited to "supported credentials" and is additive rather than mandatory, so not every credential is shown to be covered. missing for 10: evidence that keys are kept out of chat/session history, detail on how scrubbing works and what it applies to, the full list of credentials SecretRefs support, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, credentials are handled deliberately — a secrets store or env separation with redaction, never API keys pasted into chat history

citations.quote: OpenClaw supports additive SecretRefs so supported credentials do not need to live as plaintext in configuration.
Secrets management: SecretRef contract, shared secret store, runtime snapshots, and safe one-way scrubbing
A cell is a full Gateway in a hardened container with its own state, credentials, workspace, channel accounts, token, and loopback-only host port.
You want multiple agents with separate workspaces, auth, and sessions in one Gateway process.
